answer: Spectral-gap analysis resists sybils: the honest trust graph has a large spectral gap (fast information spread), but a sybil cluster bolted on via a thin cut collapses that gap — the second eigenvalue betrays the bottleneck. A plume of fakes hanging off the karst by few edges shows up as a near-disconnected component in the graph's spectrum. Influence weighted by spectral centrality starves a region that sits past the knoll of the bottleneck, because the math of the cut cannot be hidden however densely the fakes interlink.
